messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: choosing cut points
parts:
> > I have a question concerning the choice of cutpoints when grouping data.
> >
> > is it better to choose rounded cutpoints values (i e 10 m, 20m 30m ..) or

> > to choose a fixed number of intervals, with decimal values of cutpoints ?.
> > we have an example for wich with the same number of intervals, and the same

> > function, the GOF test and the CV are better in the second case.
> > visually, the adjustment curves seems similar..
> >

> > I think I do not have heaping problem, as rangefinders (precision 1m) were used

If you don't have a problem with heaping, then you're really only choosing
cutpoints for visual presentation of the data and model fits. Distance 4
has goodness-of-fit tests that don't require you to group the data
(Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Cramer-von Mises). I would use those, in which
case choice of intervals isn't important. (If there were heaping, I would
choose cutpoints well away from the distances at which observations are
heaped.)

Steve Buckland
